kisera yābe — "what is lost [by it]". belādhika — "when the day has [too far] advanced". The sense of the last line: Narahari has given warning, and there will be nothing to blame him for.

verses_en.text:
Wake up, thief of people's hearts, best of the clever, beautiful One who sports in the town of Nadia!
Radha is the crest-jewel of women, full of rasa: You are the delight of the treasure of Her heart.
What shall I say? Again and again [I tell You]: the night has turned to dawn.
What laziness is this? I understand nothing — many doubts [remain] in my heart. (Refrain)*
When You hear of the lovely deeds and virtues [of the people] of Vraja, neither food nor sleep pleases You;
while telling [of them], You do not distinguish(?) day from night — so how can sleep please You now?
The matchless sankirtana, the root of happiness, You always hold dearer than life;
without it a moment is for You like a kalpa. At this, Narahari's mind is bewildered.*
Manjumukhi-chhandah
notes: The first four lines in the edition are the refrain (the dhru mark at the page edge is worn away; OCR — "ঞ]"). Gaura is called the beloved of Radha: He is Krishna Himself (cf. note 31). tākara hṛdaya-ratana-rucikārī — understood as "giving delight to the treasure of Her heart"; possibly "the lovely treasure of Her heart".

Reading unclear: bāchahe(?) (the third letter is indistinct; OCR — bahe) — understood as "distinguish". Sankirtana — the congregational singing of the Lord's names and pastimes, held each night in the house of Srivasa (cf. 1.61). A kalpa is a day of Brahma, an immense span of time (cf. note 5).

verses_en.text:
The very skilful parrot spoke much in this way.
Gaura in His sleep heard a little, intoxicated with rasa.
Seeing that the bed was grieved, He who gives joy to all
stretched a little — and remained [lying]: He cannot leave [it].*
Raga yatharaga
notes: The parrot is the one raised by the Lord's servant (2.15a). mori — "stretching". "The bed was grieved" — because the Lord was about to leave it.

verses_en.text:
Languid and limp, the Lord, crest-jewel of rasikas, speaks, as if in a dream, words full of rasa:
"Bereft of the rasa of seeing Radha-ramana, [My] life is burning, burning away in fever.*
Listen, Gauri, Haridasa, Dhananjaya, Sanjaya, Vijaya, Mukunda, Murari,
Madhava, Vasudeva, Purushottama, Shridhara, Krishnadasa who gives joy,
Shrinidhi, Madhusudana, Vakreshvara, Satyaraja, wise Kavichandra,
Shankara, Garuda, Bhagavata, Nandana, Chandrashekhara, profound Saranga,
Shuklambara, Yadunatha, Nakula, Vanamali, Mahesha, Shrinidhi — abode of virtues!*
Providence, most kind, understanding My heart, has given Me unceasing company with all of you.
Therefore, accepting My humble request — that [narrative] full of the rasa of the lovely deeds of the people of Vraja —
sing it with brilliance in sweet ragas, and remove this cruel burning of [My] heart.*
How much more shall I reveal what is hidden in My heart? These mighty wicked enemies have made [Me] their subject.
I took this body in vain, I have understood nothing; I have become [one wandering] without a path, [poor] in the fullness of prema(?).*
Again, joining My palms, I say: all of you together, gladly fulfil the heart's desire of your own [dear one]:
birth after birth, without obstruction, may I be in this world a servant of the lotus feet of the Lord of the gopis."*
Having spoken such words, the king of the twice-born, sinking again a little into sleep, fell silent.
Narahari is bewildered: he cannot in the least describe [these] matchless lovely deeds, rare even for the gods.*
Chatushpadi-chhandah
notes: Radha-ramana ("the delight of Radha") is Krishna. Whereas in 2.13–2.14 Gaura in His sleep spoke the words of Krishna, here He speaks in the mood of Radha separated from Krishna: Gaura is Krishna who has accepted Radha's mood in order to taste Her love (cf. notes 14, 31). jara jara jīu jīu jari yāta — lit. "the life, all in fever, burns away".

A list of the Lord's associates in Navadvipa; the identifications are tentative: Gauri — probably Gauridasa Pandita (possibly the address "O Gauri"); Haridasa; Dhananjaya Pandita; Sanjaya (Mukunda-Sanjaya, in whose house Nimai taught); Vijaya (Vijaya Dasa the copyist?); Mukunda Datta; Murari Gupta; Madhava and Vasudeva (Ghosha); Shridhara (the seller of banana-leaf cups); Shrinidhi; Vakreshvara Pandita; Satyaraja Khan; Kavichandra; Shankara Pandita; Garuda Pandita; Bhagavata Acharya; Nandana Acharya; Chandrashekhara Acharya; Saranga (Sharnga Murari?); Shuklambara Brahmachari; Yadunatha; Nakula Brahmachari; Vanamali Pandita; Mahesha Pandita. The name Shrinidhi is repeated in the list (lines 5 and 7) — so in the edition.

"Providence" (vihi, vidhi) — the Creator, destiny. parabhāga — "excellence, brilliance": to sing with the highest art. Cf. CC Antya: in separation from Krishna, Mahaprabhu was consoled with songs and verses by Svarupa Damodara and Ramananda Raya.

"Wicked enemies" (khala ripu) — the six inner enemies (the evil qualities of the mind). These are words of humility (dainya) spoken by the Lord in the mood of a devotee; cf. the Shikshashtaka (CC Antya 20). Reading and sense unclear: prema-bharāti — understood as "[poor] in the fullness of prema"; possibly "in an excess of prema".
sukha-sañe — "gladly". The Lord of the gopis (gopī-pati) is Krishna. Cf. the Shikshashtaka (CC Antya 20): the prayer for service to Krishna's feet birth after birth.
"King of the twice-born" (dvija-kula-bhūpa) — Gaura, born in a brahmana family. dulaha — durlabha, "hard to attain".

verses_en.text: Who can tell [this] lovely lila to its end?
